scenes.title: Indignation, Envy and Pity
scenes.summary: Opposed to pity is indignation, pain at undeserved good fortune; both belong to good character, and we ascribe indignation to the gods. Envy seems close to it but differs, being pain at the success of one's like; the opposite feelings follow, and all of them hinder pity.

scenes.title: At What People Are Indignant
scenes.summary: Indignation is felt not at virtue but at wealth, power and the like, more at new wealth than old, at goods that do not suit their holder, and when the inferior contends with the superior, as Hector avoided battle with Ajax.

scenes.title: Who Is Prone to Indignation
scenes.summary: Those worthy of the greatest goods and possessing them, the good and those fond of honor are prone to indignation; the slavish and those indifferent to honor are not. A speech that shows the claimants of pity undeserving makes pity impossible.
